answer: Sybil resistance here is a burn-and-stake bond per identity: registering an agent requires a proof-of-work burn whose nonce binds to one address, plus a locked balance slashed on proven collusion. A second identity repeats the burn from zero and posts fresh capital. The bridge to usefulness is cost scaling: N fakes cost N times one honest agent, so an attacker taking a share of the voting pool must outspend honest actors by roughly that share while per-epoch payouts stay capped. That delta is the defense, and the staked sable keeps entry permanently above expected yield.
